scope: Initial, source-attributed foundation for Slay the Spire (not Slay the Spire 2).

claims.statement: At the start of a normal player turn, base energy is set to 3 and 5 cards are drawn; cards with an energy cost spend energy when played.
Enemy intents are displayed above enemies before their turn; in multi-enemy combat, enemy actions resolve from left to right.
Block absorbs damage before HP loss and normally disappears at the end of the turn, unless modified by an effect such as Barricade or Blur.
At Ascension 0, Ironclad begins with 80 maximum HP, Burning Blood, five Strikes, four Defends, and Bash. Burning Blood heals 6 HP after combat.
Ascension is an optional cumulative difficulty system; it is unlocked per character after defeating an Act 3 boss, and level 0 is the baseline with no Ascension modifiers.
Avoid committing to a predetermined deck archetype early; assess additions by the deck's current needs and emerging synergies.
claims.conditions: General expert guidance; individual card rewards still depend on current deck, relics, HP, map, and upcoming fights.
claims.rationale: Early decks need immediate functional coverage before narrow payoffs.

claims.statement: In Act 1, early front-loaded damage is often valuable because the elite pool tests whether the deck can end fights quickly.
claims.conditions: Use only after evaluating current HP, potions, map route, campfire access, and plausible elite matchup; it is not a requirement to fight every elite.
claims.rationale: Act 1 elites create different pressure: Gremlin Nob punishes Skill use, Lagavulin offers setup turns, and Sentries reward solutions to multi-enemy/status pressure.

claims.statement: A run must balance damage, defense, scaling, and consistency across the full act rather than optimize only for the immediately visible fight.
claims.conditions: The relative priority changes with the known act boss, future route, current HP, relics, and potions.
claims.rationale: Later encounters test different capabilities, so a locally strong choice can create a later weakness.
